svg.text: Failover: discovering a dead node's sessions (no COMMIT message)
The successor learns it owns S when its own CAS succeeds. Every survivor computes the same HRW split, so no coordination is needed.
t
D's last heartbeat
0 s · D crashes
claim threshold (15 s): D's leases not yet claimable
15 s · claimable
next roster poll
≤ 20 s · detect
claim · rehydrate · reconcile
~18–26 s · resumed
Trigger 1 · roster detects death → bounded, split query
SELECT … FROM bcs_task_leases
WHERE node_id = :D AND has_pending_work
AND bucket IN (:mine) LIMIT 2000
:mine = buckets ranking me first without D
1 batch per poll (1 s while backlog); 3 s grace
pending work = non-terminal run · queued delivery ·
durable timer · unprocessed inbound input
idle sessions are left alone
Trigger 2 · claim on demand
An idle session's next round finds the owner dead
(forward fails / roster says stale) → preferred survivor claims
and serves. Not yet claimable → durable fallback → Trigger 1.
Trigger 3 · safety-net sweep (30–60 s)
Released or dead-owned leases with pending work:
catches failed claims, nodes that were restarting, etc.
Taking over earlier on evidence (fencing makes a wrong guess safe; it only costs a rehydration)
Same advertise_addr, new node_id — the process restarted in place; two processes can't listen on one address → old run's leases
claimable as soon as the new roster row is seen. RTO ≈ restart time + ≤ 5 s.
Mark own roster row dead on panic — leases kept, so survivors find them at once; best effort (not on OOM kill / kill -9).
Relative staleness — stale(D) = max(heartbeats) − heartbeat(D), plus a recovery grace: nobody claims until its own heartbeats are healthy for 15 s.
A node that is alive but silently unreachable gives no evidence: wait the claim threshold.
